question: to the Commission Erik Marquardt (Verts/ALE), Majdouline Sbai (Verts/ALE), Saskia Bricmont (Verts/ALE), Tineke Strik (Verts/ALE), Jan-Christoph Oetjen (Renew), Rudi Kennes (The Left), Merja Kyllönen (The Left), Cecilia Strada (S&D), Hanna Gedin (The Left), Damien Carême (The Left), Daniel Freund (Verts/ALE), Murielle Laurent (S&D), Birgit Sippel (S&D), Konstantinos Arvanitis (The Left) Subject:

A serious incident report of Frontex’s Fundamental Rights Office1 reveals that on 22 June 2023, Greek authorities used Afghan paramilitaries to violently push a group of 61 asylum seekers, including 11 children, back to Türkiye over the Evros, while subjecting them to inhuman treatment. The pushback was done by three Greek police officers and 10-20 masked, armed third-country nationals, reported to be Afghan paramilitaries. The Fundamental Rights Office concludes that they acted under the instruction and effective control of the Greek authorities, and describes the use of mercenaries in pushbacks as ‘a matter of coordinated policy’ in the Evros region. The Greek authorities have denied this incident. 1.

Is the Commission or Frontex aware of collaboration with, or use of, mercenaries or paramilitaries from Afghanistan or other third countries by the Greek authorities in the context of pushbacks? Are other cases of such collaboration known, and if so how many, and does this constitute an official or de facto policy of the Greek authorities? Please share any information at the disposal of Frontex or the Commission.

What measures will the Commission take to hold the Greek authorities accountable for these pushbacks, to ensure swift further investigation of this incident by the Greek authorities, and to eliminate the systematic practice of both Greek collaboration with foreign paramilitaries on pushbacks and of the pushbacks themselves?
SIR 13125/2023, https://prd.frontex.europa.eu/document/serious-incident-reports-cat-1-2/.
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (19.6.2026) The Commission is aware of the report of the European Border and Coast Guard Agency’s (Frontex) Fundamental Rights Office concerning the referred incident of 22 June 2023. The Commission cannot confirm the existence of similar cases or the existence of an official or de facto policy involving collaboration with paramilitary or mercenary actors. The Commission considers all allegations of violations of fundamental rights at the EU’s external borders to be a matter of concern, which is subject to investigation by the competent national authorities. The Commission recalls that all border management activities need to comply with the relevant EU law, the Charter of Fundamental Rights and the principle of non-refoulement. The Commission remains in contact with the Greek authorities and with Frontex regarding these allegations.
